findings.highlight: You're biting the hand that's feeding you.
findings.explanation: Sayuri tells Mihoko that she is directing unjustified resentment at Koharu. The English accuses her of betraying a benefactor, inventing a dependence or favor relationship rather than identifying misplaced blame.
findings.japanese:
「いい加減にしときなよ矢田。
それって逆恨みだよ」
findings.todokanai: "Stop being unreasonable, Yada. You're biting the hand that's feeding you."

findings.highlight: I have the morning shift at Goodies with Sugiura on Saturday and Sunday.
findings.evidenceJa: 今週土曜日は、杉浦がグッディーズの早番。日曜も同様
findings.explanation: Haruki's schedule calculation says Sugiura has the early Goodies shift on both Saturday and Sunday. The English says Haruki has those shifts with her, assigning him work he is merely considering visiting around.
findings.japanese:
毎週金曜日は、開桜社のバイト。
今週土曜日は、杉浦がグッディーズの早番。
日曜も同様。
findings.todokanai: I have part-time work at Kaiou Graph tonight. And I have the morning shift at Goodies with Sugiura on Saturday and Sunday.

findings.highlight: They've been rushing me on this since yesterday!
findings.evidenceJa: こっちは本当は昨日がデッドだった
findings.explanation: Hamada admits his real deadline was yesterday. The English instead says other people have been rushing him since yesterday, deleting the fact that his assignment is already overdue.
findings.japanese:
「何ぃ？　お前上司に向かって生意気だぞ！
こっちは本当は昨日がデッドだったんだからな！」
findings.todokanai: "What's that? Is that the kind of attitude you should have when talking to your superior!? They've been rushing me on this since yesterday!"

findings.highlight: a speech that could lead to a huge misunderstanding
findings.evidenceJa: 勘違いも甚だしい発言だったかも
findings.explanation: Mari regrets that her encouragement may itself have been founded on a severe misunderstanding of Haruki. The English says her speech might cause someone else to misunderstand, reversing whether misunderstanding produced or resulted from the statement.
findings.japanese:
「その、偉そうだった上に、
勘違いも甚だしい発言だったかもと、
その後反省しきりで...」
findings.todokanai: "About… me acting all high and mighty, and making a speech that could lead to a huge misunderstanding. I thought about that afterward…"

findings.highlight: it feels very awkward to talk about it
findings.evidenceJa: なんとなく言わずにはおれなかった
findings.explanation: Mari says several things overlapped with her own experience, so she somehow could not help saying the advice. The English says the overlap made it awkward to talk, reversing an irresistible impulse to speak into reluctance.
findings.japanese:
「ちょっと色々オーバーラップするところがあって、
なんとなく言わずにはおれなかったというか...」
findings.todokanai: "Since there are so many coincidences overlapping, it feels very awkward to talk about it…"

findings.explanation: After thinking he cannot ask such an intrusive question “yet,” Haruki catches and questions his own use of “yet.” The English makes him wonder what Mari means, assigning his revealing self-correction to her.

findings.highlight: the gentle winter sun finally came to melt it once and for all
findings.evidenceJa: そこにまた、冬の優しい日射しが降り注いでくれたから
findings.explanation: Haruki imagines gentle winter sunlight falling again on snow that thawed and then refroze harder; the line does not say it has now melted. The English declares it melted once and for all, converting tentative renewed warmth into completed permanent healing.
findings.japanese:
解けかけた雪が夜に凍結し、
前よりも固く凍りついてしまったけれど、
そこにまた、冬の優しい日射しが降り注いでくれたから？
findings.todokanai: Is it because the terrible cold of night revitalized the snow which was on the verge of finally melting, forming ice even colder than before, but then the gentle winter sun finally came to melt it once and for all?

findings.evidenceJa: もう終わったことだって言いましたよね
findings.explanation: Haruki repeats that the relationship or event is over, a claim the surrounding chapter distinguishes from its emotional aftermath. “I've moved on” asserts inner resolution that his narration and continued pain explicitly do not support.
findings.japanese:
「いいですよ、そんなに気を使わなくて。
もう終わったことだって言いましたよね」
findings.todokanai: "It's fine, don't worry about it. Like I said before, I've moved on already."

findings.highlight: thinking about making this amazing burger
findings.evidenceJa: 超絶バーガー頼むこともある
findings.explanation: Mari says she sometimes splurges by ordering the Superlative Burger, whose drawback is how long it takes to arrive. The English says she is thinking of making an amazing burger and that cooking it takes too long, changing takeout or service into home preparation.
findings.japanese:
「最近はちょっと贅沢に
超絶バーガー頼むこともあるけど、
あれ、出てくるのに時間かかるのが難点ね」
findings.todokanai: "I was thinking about making this amazing burger lately, but the problem with making it is that it would take too much time…"

findings.evidenceJa: 左右にブレてきたわね
findings.explanation: At the batting center, Sawako says Mari's hits are beginning to scatter left and right, evidence that she is nearing her limit. The English says Mari's body is swaying, replacing declining batting accuracy with physical instability.
findings.japanese:
「左右にブレてきたわね。
そろそろ限界じゃない？」
findings.todokanai: "She's swaying left and right. Are you at your limit already?"

findings.highlight: "She's a good person. Even though I hate to admit it. She's a very cute woman. Just a little stubborn. So promise not to abandon her?"
findings.evidenceJa:
「あいつ、いい奴なのよ。むかつくけど。
可愛い女なのよ。やってられないけど。
だから、捨てないでやってね？」
findings.explanation: Sawako's “I can't stand it” aside becomes “just a little stubborn,” changing her affectionate complaint into a trait assigned to Mari.
findings.japanese:
「あいつ、いい奴なのよ。むかつくけど。
可愛い女なのよ。やってられないけど。
だから、捨てないでやってね？」
findings.todokanai: "She's a good person. Even though I hate to admit it. She's a very cute woman. Just a little stubborn. So promise not to abandon her?"

findings.highlight: shows that she's interested in this topic
findings.evidenceJa: あからさまに面白くなさそうな表情
findings.explanation: Sawako listens with an openly displeased or unamused expression and seems unwilling to accept Haruki's account. The English says her face shows interest, reversing the affect that motivates her argumentative refusal.
findings.japanese:
雨宮さんは、あからさまに面白くなさそうな表情で、
俺の話す事実を受け入れがたそうに聞いている。
findings.todokanai: Amamiya-san's expression shows that she's interested in this topic, but she doesn't seem to believe what I'm telling her.

findings.evidenceJa: その上で麻理はあなたを選ぶと思う
findings.explanation: Sawako says she thinks Mari would choose Haruki even after taking age and character into account. The English makes that hypothetical judgment a completed past choice, prematurely confirming the romance Haruki is denying.
findings.japanese:
「もちろんその通りよ。
その上で麻理はあなたを選ぶと思うんだけどなぁ」
findings.todokanai: "Well, of course, that's exactly right. But I still think Mari chose you because she sees more in you beyond that."

findings.highlight: given the fact that she's walking alone
findings.evidenceJa: 足取りとか見てると、ちっとも酔ってるようには見えない
findings.explanation: Haruki judges from Mari's gait that she does not look drunk at all. The English says this is because she is walking alone, replacing the observed steadiness of her steps with an irrelevant social fact.
findings.japanese:
足取りとか見てると、
ちっとも酔ってるようには見えないけどな。
findings.todokanai: But given the fact that she's walking alone, I wouldn't be able to tell if she's drunk at all.

findings.highlight: we'll probably feel really awkward if she still remembers
findings.evidenceJa: 今度は今日のことを思い出して、気まずい思いを抱えてそうだ
findings.explanation: Haruki predicts that when sober Mari next sees him, she will remember today's behavior and carry embarrassment. The English turns this into mutual awkwardness conditional on whether she remembers, changing both subject and certainty.
findings.japanese:
これでまた素面の時に顔を合わせたら、
今度は今日のことを思い出して、
気まずい思いを抱えてそうだ。
findings.todokanai: At this rate, when we see each other next time, we'll probably feel really awkward if she still remembers what happened today.

findings.highlight: I couldn't understand the hidden messages
findings.evidenceJa: 親友同士の認識の溝は埋まらず
findings.explanation: The unresolved gap is between the two best friends' interpretations of which woman became carried away. The English instead says Haruki failed to understand hidden messages, relocating the disagreement into his private comprehension.
findings.japanese: 結局、親友同士の認識の溝は埋まらずか。
findings.todokanai: As a result, I couldn't understand the hidden messages between these two best friends after all.

findings.explanation: Haruki says there are about thirty minutes until the first train. The English says they are thirty minutes away from the station, turning a waiting time into travel distance and obscuring why Mari chooses a taxi.
findings.japanese: 「始発まであと３０分くらいありますけど？」
findings.todokanai: "Aren't we still 30 minutes away from the station?"

findings.highlight: Suzuki sent me a text earlier
findings.evidenceJa: さっき鈴木にメール入れたら、元気な泣き言が返ってきた
findings.explanation: Mari says she texted Suzuki and received an energetic complaint in reply. The English says Suzuki initiated the earlier text, reversing who contacted whom as Mari decides to return and help the office.
findings.japanese:
「さっき鈴木にメール入れたら、
元気な泣き言が返ってきたからね」
findings.todokanai: "Suzuki sent me a text earlier, she's practically crying for me to come back and help."
